method: Inclusion is every taxon printed under the Vespertilionidae heading on the 2011 Wayback SANParks KNP mammal checklist PDF except Miniopterus schreibersii, which is stored under Miniopteridae following the Phase 1 family remap (20 taxa printed under that heading, 19 remaining after the move). English and Afrikaans names, and species order, are taken from that PDF. Scientific names are the 2011 names unless an iNaturalist taxon record cited in remaps gives a current name. Eptesicus melckorum is printed as a separate species on the 2011 list but is an invalid scientific name of Laephotis capensis on iNaturalist, so it is recorded as a remap of the included Cape serotine and is not given a second species row (18 stored species). Research-grade counts are for iNaturalist place_id 69020. iNaturalist-only vespertilionids are in candidates, not species. The PDF was fetched to a temporary path for text extraction and was not copied into this project.

notes: An iNaturalist taxa search for the 2011 name matches Scotophilus borbonicus (taxon 40441), which remains an active species and lists no invalid scientific names. Scotophilus viridis (taxon 40433, preferred_common_name Greenish House Bat) is a separate active species; its name list does not include S. borbonicus. Observation total_results is 0 for both, and neither appears in the place taxonomy tree (the tree has 18 observations of any grade under genus Scotophilus, of which 5 are S. dinganii and 13 are at genus rank). Because it is unclear whether the 2011 Kruger taxon should be limited to S. borbonicus or referred to S. viridis, and there are no species-rank Kruger records to decide it, the stored latin value is the 2011 name.

Eptesicus melckorum is printed as a separate official species, but iNaturalist treats that name as an invalid scientific name of the included Laephotis capensis. It was not given a second species row. The 2011 English and Afrikaans names for Melck's serotine bat are recorded only in that remap note.

An iNaturalist taxa search for the 2011 trinomial Eptesicus somalicus zuluensis returned 0 results. The elevation to Neoromicia zuluensis rests on the printed synonym Eptesicus zuluensis. That missing trinomial link is logged. Neoromicia somalica, which carries the parent epithet, has 0 research-grade observations in place 69020 and was not added as a candidate.

Owner question: Scotophilus borbonicus remains an active iNaturalist species and is the stored 2011 name, but S. viridis is a separate active species with no synonym link to S. borbonicus. Neither has species-rank Kruger records (0 research-grade, absent from the tree). Many place observations are identified only to genus Scotophilus (13 of any grade at genus rank).

Searches for the exact 2011 spelling Glauconycteris variegatus, and for the printed synonym Nycticeius schlieffenii, returned 0 results. Remaps rest on name lists reached via the printed synonym or the close spelling that iNaturalist does list.

Most official vespertilionids have 0 research-grade iNaturalist observations in place 69020. The only official taxa with a research-grade count above 0 are Scotophilus dinganii (4), Myotis welwitschii (1), Afronycteris nanus (1), and Cnephaeus hottentotus (1). Absence of an iNat record was not treated as absence from KNP.

No rare, reintroduced, or introduced flags are recorded for official Vespertilionidae species: the 2011 PDF does not mark any of them with an asterisk or other status note (asterisks on that list are only for house mouse and house/black rat under Muridae).
Candidate Afrikaans names were left null. The Phase 2 rule was to take af from the 2011 SANParks checklist; these taxa are not on that list.
The current live official list, Skinner & Chimimba, and Stuart's guide were not available to corroborate remaps or flags.
